protected_proposition: Wave 3 cannot be the shortest among Waves 1, 3 and 5.

semantic_findings.paraphrased_finding: Wave 3 may or may not be longest, but it may not be shortest among Waves 1, 3 and 5.

The rule is described as comparing price movement, and the Volume 10 answer says both arithmetic and percentage terms apply conceptually; neither basis is presented as merely optional or illustrative.
A developing Wave 5 can definitively invalidate the proposed count as soon as it becomes longer than Wave 3 when Wave 1 is already longer than Wave 3.

Connected schematic wave turns are shown, but the sources do not identify which observable price field defines each start/end or distinguish orthodox endpoint, extreme, intrabar extreme, close, or another observation.
semantic_findings.exact_question: Which source-authorized observed-price fields define the start and end of Waves 1, 3 and 5?
reviewed_source_states: Volume 1 formal and applied discussions show schematic turns but do not bind them to an observable price field.
Volume 10 P005 discussion is silent on endpoint observation type.

semantic_findings.paraphrased_finding: Arithmetic treatment is named, but no exact magnitude/sign formula, units, normalization, or downward-direction operation is given.
